IS: 7734. 1975 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

FORCEPS, EYE, PERIPHERAL IRIDECTOMY, 

TRAQUAIR'S PATTERN 



1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for Traquair's pattern peripheral iridectomy forceps used 
in eye surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 and 2. 



-JAW A 




PIN.DIA 1 -s ™ 
^SUITABLE TRANSVERSE GROOVES ENLARGED 

FOR HOLDING SECTION Y Y 

♦See Fig. 2 for details of jaws. 

All dimensions In millimetres. 
FIG. 1 FORCEPS, EYE, PERIPHERAL IRIDECTOMY, TRAQUAIR'S PATTERN 

2.1 Joint — Block or semi-block type, conforming to the requirements laid down in 5 of IS : 3642-1966 
' General requirements for surgical instruments '. 

3. Materials — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 20Cr1 3 or 30Cr1 3 of IS : 6603- 1 972 ' Speci- 
fication for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

3.1 Check pins shall be of stainless steel conforming to Designation 04Cr18Ni10 or C7Cr18Ni9 of 
IS: 6603-1972. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The forceps shall be finished smooth and free from burrs, pits, cracks, etc. 

4.2 The edges shall be even and slightly rounded except the teeth which shall be pointed The teeth 
of the forceps on closure, shall interlock with accuracy and precision and on release the forceps shall 
open fully without catching. 

4.3 The grooves on the arms shall be uniform and shall have a proper grip to the fingers and shall not 
be sharp. 

4.4 The riveting or the spot welding of the joint shall be neat and sound. 

4.5 The forceps shall be polished bright and passivated. 

5. Heat Treatment — The arms of the forceps shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 
380 to 430 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Performance — A latex sheet of 005 mm thickness shall be stretched over the tip of a finger. The 
stretched latex sheet shall then be gripped by the teeth of the forceps and pulled to a distance of about 
5 mm. The forceps shall hold the latex sheet firmly without any tendency of slipping and the latex 
sheet shall not be punctured. 



Adopted 23 July 1975 



October 1975, ISI

All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 2 DETAILS OF JAWS A AND B 

6.2 Flexibility — A strip of vulcanized rubber 2 mm thick shall be placed in between the arms at the 
angled portion of the forceps leaving the teeth free. An attempt shall be made to close the forceps by 
means of thumb and finger of one hand. On release of the pressure, the forceps shall show no sign 
of damage and shall continue to satisfy the requirements laid down in 4.2 and 6.1. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance — The instrument shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test as mentioned in 
IS : 7531-1975 ' Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel 
surgical instruments '. 

7. Marking — Each instrument shall be marked with either the manufacturer's name or initials or trade- 
mark, the letters ' SS ' and the country of manufacture. 

7.1 l$t Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, however, the teeth of the forceps 
shall be suitably protected. To protect the forceps from damage, 8 ring made of plastic or rubber tubing 
of suitable dimensions shall be provided for closing the forceps, when not in use.
